[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction
[原文]
Mechanical, chemical, and biological treatments are usually adopted to obtain the desired physical and mechanical properties and for further utilization of the natural cellulosic fibers. Therein, Papirindustriens forskningsinstitut (PFI) refining is the most common laboratory refiner in order to improve the inter-fiber bonding capacity [1] and accessibility [2,3], and manufacture the micro-fibrillated or nano-fibrillated cellulose [4–6]. The main efects of PFI refining on fibers are: (i) internal fibrillation—delaminating, loosening, and swelling of fiber wall; (ii) external fibrillation—peeling of fibrils from the fiber surface while remaining attached; (iii) fiber shortening—fiber cutting due to shearing action, and (iv) fines formation—primary fines come from ray cells and parenchyma cells and microfibrils that are caused by fiber shortening or external fibrillation. Moreover, the PFI refining could be adopted to obtain a higher internal fibrillation than other laboratory refiners [1]. These efects of the PFI refining on cellulosic fibers will improve the accessibility, the swelling, the flexibility, and the inter-fiber bonding capacity of fibers.

[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction
[原文]
 It is assumed that these changes in the macro-level structure and properties are related to the changes of crystallinity and H-bonding network during refining [7,8].

There are some diferent conclusions regarding to the efects of PFI refining on crystallinity of cellulose, not like that of ball milling, which efectively reduces the crystallinity as the treatment progresses. Although some researchers considered that the crystallinity decreased during PFI refining for corn stover [9] or softwood pulp [10], some researchers reported that the crystallinity increased first and then decreased with the degree of refining for hardwood bleached kraft pulp fibers [11] or for unbleached eucalyptus fibers [12]. Moreover, Zhao et al. [7] reported that the crystallinity initially fluctuated upward and then downward, followed by a repeating fluctuation with PFI refining for tobacco stem mechanical pulp. None of the previous studies identified a clear trend, but the results were that the crystallinity varied during PFI refinement. Based on the large proportion of H-bonds in crystalline region of cellulose, it can be assumed that the H-bonding network might change during PFI refining.

[原文]
Fourier transformation infrared spectroscopy (FT-IR), which is sensitive to molecular structure, can be as an indirect measurement for studying H-bonding network. FT-IR deconvolution of hydroxyl groups band was adopted in order to study the changes of the energy of H-bonds and the H-bonding distance during delignification [13] or the deconstruction of cellulose [14]. Moreover, it was used to study the diferences of the content of H-bonds not only between dislocation region and normal region [15], but also among plant species [16,17]. Regarding the changes of H-bonding network during PFI refining, Yuan et al. [18] reported that the content of H-bonds and crystallinity index (CI) of eucalyptus fibers changed with the increment of beating time. Subsequently, Zhao et al. [8] found that the H-bonding energy for O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>) inter-molecular H-bonds decreased by 12.9% and evolutions of the content of certain H-bonds difered at various refining stages.

[原文]
There is still a lack of literature on the efects of PFI refinement on the H-bonding network. Particularly, the relationship between the content of H-bonds and crystallinity is still worthy of further study, which will deepen the understanding of the molecular aggregation and distribution of H-bonds, providing a molecular-scale explanation for the variations in accessibility, swelling, flexibility, and fibrillation of cellulosic fibers during PFI refinement. Therefore, this work explored the efects of PFI refinement on the CI, crystallite size, energy of H-bonds, H-bonding distance, and content of H-bonds for softwood pulp fibers and hardwood pulp fibers. Attempts were made in order to establish the correlations between the CI and content of various H-bonds.

It had an increase of 3.5% from 31.4% to 32.5% in the stage of refining from 0 r to 4000 r and it then decreased by 21.57% from 4000 r to 12000 r, along with a growth of 15.26% in the last refining stage. For the content of the O(2)H· · · O(6) H-bonds of hardwood fiber, it increased firstly and then had a decrease that was also followed by an increase. [章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 3. Results and Discussions > 3.3. Efect of PFI Refining on H-Bonding Energies, H-Bonding Distances, and Content of H-Bonds
[原文]
As to the free OH(2) and OH(6) of softwood fiber, the relative content showed a slight increase trend in general. The enhancement of the free OH(2) and OH(6) was understandable, because there was the breakage of H-bonds among cellulosic molecules, which resulted in more extensive delamination and higher specific surface area (as shown in Figure S4 and Table S1 in Online Resource). This made cellulose more accessible to water and chemicals. However, for the free OH(2) and OH(6) of hardwood fiber, the number of the free OH(2) and OH(6) decreased by 21.65% from 14.32% to 11.22%, with revolutions increasing from 0 r to 4000 r, followed by an increase of 45.37% in the stage of refining from 4000 r to 12,000 r, along with an decrease of 17.11%. It could be explained by the instability of free OH groups, which makes it easy to form new H-bonds, such as O(2)H· · · O(6) or O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>)H-bonds. Thus although there is the formation of free OH(2) and OH(6) during fibrillation, the content of the free OH(2) and OH(6) might disease; meanwhile, the content of the O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>) or the O(2)H· · · O(6) H-bonds might increase upon drying.

[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction
[原文]
Mechanical, chemical, and biological treatments are usually adopted to obtain the desired physical and mechanical properties and for further utilization of the natural cellulosic fibers. Therein, Papirindustriens forskningsinstitut (PFI) refining is the most common laboratory refiner in order to improve the inter-fiber bonding capacity [1] and accessibility [2,3], and manufacture the micro-fibrillated or nano-fibrillated cellulose [4–6]. The main efects of PFI refining on fibers are: (i) internal fibrillation—delaminating, loosening, and swelling of fiber wall; (ii) external fibrillation—peeling of fibrils from the fiber surface while remaining attached; (iii) fiber shortening—fiber cutting due to shearing action, and (iv) fines formation—primary fines come from ray cells and parenchyma cells and microfibrils that are caused by fiber shortening or external fibrillation. Moreover, the PFI refining could be adopted to obtain a higher internal fibrillation than other laboratory refiners [1]. These efects of the PFI refining on cellulosic fibers will improve the accessibility, the swelling, the flexibility, and the inter-fiber bonding capacity of fibers.

[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction
[原文]
 It is assumed that these changes in the macro-level structure and properties are related to the changes of crystallinity and H-bonding network during refining [7,8].

There are some diferent conclusions regarding to the efects of PFI refining on crystallinity of cellulose, not like that of ball milling, which efectively reduces the crystallinity as the treatment progresses. Although some researchers considered that the crystallinity decreased during PFI refining for corn stover [9] or softwood pulp [10], some researchers reported that the crystallinity increased first and then decreased with the degree of refining for hardwood bleached kraft pulp fibers [11] or for unbleached eucalyptus fibers [12]. Moreover, Zhao et al. [7] reported that the crystallinity initially fluctuated upward and then downward, followed by a repeating fluctuation with PFI refining for tobacco stem mechanical pulp. None of the previous studies identified a clear trend, but the results were that the crystallinity varied during PFI refinement. Based on the large proportion of H-bonds in crystalline region of cellulose, it can be assumed that the H-bonding network might change during PFI refining.

[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction
[原文]
Fourier transformation infrared spectroscopy (FT-IR), which is sensitive to molecular structure, can be as an indirect measurement for studying H-bonding network. FT-IR deconvolution of hydroxyl groups band was adopted in order to study the changes of the energy of H-bonds and the H-bonding distance during delignification [13] or the deconstruction of cellulose [14]. Moreover, it was used to study the diferences of the content of H-bonds not only between dislocation region and normal region [15], but also among plant species [16,17]. Regarding the changes of H-bonding network during PFI refining, Yuan et al. [18] reported that the content of H-bonds and crystallinity index (CI) of eucalyptus fibers changed with the increment of beating time. Subsequently, Zhao et al. [8] found that the H-bonding energy for O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>) inter-molecular H-bonds decreased by 12.9% and evolutions of the content of certain H-bonds difered at various refining stages.

[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction
[原文]
There is still a lack of literature on the efects of PFI refinement on the H-bonding network. Particularly, the relationship between the content of H-bonds and crystallinity is still worthy of further study, which will deepen the understanding of the molecular aggregation and distribution of H-bonds, providing a molecular-scale explanation for the variations in accessibility, swelling, flexibility, and fibrillation of cellulosic fibers during PFI refinement. Therefore, this work explored the efects of PFI refinement on the CI, crystallite size, energy of H-bonds, H-bonding distance, and content of H-bonds for softwood pulp fibers and hardwood pulp fibers. Attempts were made in order to establish the correlations between the CI and content of various H-bonds.

## 一、PFI 打浆使纸变结实的逐步过程

**第 1 步：机械作用同时产生四种效应**（该文对 PFI 打浆的归纳）[11]：
1. **内细纤维化**——纤维壁分层、疏松并润胀；
2. **外细纤维化**——表面微纤丝被剥离但仍附着于纤维；
3. **纤维切断**——剪切作用使纤维变短；
4. **细小纤维生成**——初生细小纤维来自射线细胞与薄壁细胞，另一部分由纤维切断或外细纤维化产生[11]。

**第 2 步：形态与润胀指标随之改变。** 随 PFI 转数增加（该文测试到 16,000 r），**软木浆**的宏细纤维化指数与纤维长度显著下降、细小纤维含量上升；**硬木浆**的宏细纤维化指数与纤维长度相对软木浆**无显著变化**，作者归因于硬木所用打浆压力较低[1]（细小纤维的上升趋势原文只针对软木浆陈述[1]）。同时**打浆度和 WRV 随转数显著上升**，原因是细纤维化产生了新表面与更多孔隙[6]。

**第 3 步：润胀使纤维更柔顺，从而改善纤维间结合。** WRV 所表征的润胀使纤维**横向更柔顺**，因而**有助于改善纤维网络的纤维间结合强度**[6]。分子层面：PFI 未改变氢键能量与距离（峰位几乎无红移/蓝移），但改变了各类氢键的相对含量——分子间 O(6)H···O(3′) 氢键总量软木降 16.54%、硬木降 5.91%；分子间氢键减少与结晶度下降共同提高分子链活动性、可及性与 WRV，即提高纤维柔顺性[2][9]。需注意作者同时强调：总体而言晶粒尺寸、结晶度与各类氢键含量“变化不大”，PFI 是细纤维化效果好、对超分子结构破坏较小的机械处理[12]。
**第 4 步：强度上升，而非纤维本身变强。** 零-span 抗张指数显示 **PFI 未降低纤维自身强度**；作者总结 PFI 提高了细纤维化程度（尤其是内细纤维化）、纤维润胀与纸页抗张强度，而纤维抗张强度不下降[10]。即增益主要来自**网络结合**（结合面积与柔顺性），不是单根纤维强度[10][12]。

## 二、纤维长度、细小纤维、WRV：谁贡献最大

**现有证据只支持定性分工，不支持给出贡献排名。**

- 原文最接近“主因”的表述是：**抗张强度的提升主要归因于 PFI 过程中的细纤维化和细小纤维**——二者并列，未在两者之间排序，也未把 WRV 纳入该判断[10]。
- **WRV** 在文中是**中介变量**：打浆→细纤维化/新表面→润胀（WRV↑）→横向柔顺→纤维间结合↑[6]。这是机理解释，该文并未检验 WRV 对强度的独立贡献。
- **纤维长度**的作用**因指标而异**：对**湿纸幅强度**，作者明确指出纤维长度起关键作用，并以此解释软木（纤维更长）湿纸幅强度增幅大于硬木；但同一打浆过程中软木纤维长度是**下降**的[1][10]。因此不能简单说“长度越大贡献越大”，需区分湿纸幅强度与干抗张强度、以及被打浆削短后的净效应。

**明确缺口：** 该文献未做偏相关、回归或方差分解，未报告纤维长度、细小纤维含量、WRV 对干抗张指数的标准化系数或贡献率；文中 p<0.05 的相关性只出现在结晶度指标之间（软木 r=0.919、硬木 r=0.925）[5]，与强度归因无关。故“哪个贡献最大”**无法定量回答**。就方向性而言，只能引用作者的定性判断：**细纤维化与细小纤维是抗张强度提升的主要因素 [10]，WRV 通过润胀/柔顺性起中介作用 [6]，纤维长度主要影响湿纸幅强度 [10]**——这不等同于三者的贡献排序。相关图（Figure 1–3、6–7、Table 1–2）的数值未逐点核读，上述结论均取自原文文字与表格。

- **纤维长度**的作用**因指标而异**：对**湿纸幅强度**，作者明确指出纤维长度起关键作用，并以此解释软木（纤维更长）湿纸幅强度增幅大于硬木；但同一打浆过程中软木纤维长度是**下降**的[1][10]。因此不能简单说“长度越大贡献越大”，需区分湿纸幅强度与干抗张强度、以及被打浆削短后的净效应。

**明确缺口：** 该文献未做偏相关、回归或方差分解，未报告纤维长度、细小纤维含量、WRV 对干抗张指数的标准化系数或贡献率；文中 p<0.05 的相关性只出现在结晶度指标之间（软木 r=0.919、硬木 r=0.925）[5]，与强度归因无关。故“哪个贡献最大”**无法定量回答**。就方向性而言，只能引用作者的定性判断：**细纤维化与细小纤维是抗张强度提升的主要因素 [10]，WRV 通过润胀/柔顺性起中介作用 [6]，纤维长度主要影响湿纸幅强度 [10]**——这不等同于三者的贡献排序。相关图（Figure 1–3、6–7、Table 1–2）的数值未逐点核读，上述结论均取自原文文字与表格。

**结论：现有可获取的正文证据中没有针叶木浆 8000 转时的 BET 比表面积具体数值。**

据所检索到的研究（商业漂白针叶木硫酸盐浆，PFI 打浆，浆浓 10%，打浆转数为 0、4000、8000、12000、16000 转）[4]，BET 比表面积等孔隙数据的实测结果列于**在线补充材料 Table S1**（“Cumulative pore volume, average pore size and specific surface area of softwood pulp fiber through refining”）[1]，正文未给出任何 m²/g 数值。正文只作定性表述：外部细纤维化随打浆增强，“与比表面积的增加一致（见 Online Resource 表 S1）”[10]；作者并将此归因于更高程度的细纤维化产生新表面和更多孔隙（同见表 S1）[10]——这是作者的机理解释，且为与形态学结果的定性对应关系，并非本文正文数据可直接验证的因果或定量关系。

因此：
- **8000 转的 BET 比表面积具体值须查该文补充材料 Table S1**，该补充材料不在当前可获取的证据范围内，无法给出数值，也不应推测。
- 可支持的仅是方向性表述：该文称比表面积随打浆而增加[10]；这属于文献的定性陈述，正文未给出逐点数值，故无法据此判断各转数间是否严格单调或增幅大小，也不能给出不确定度。
- 附带可核对的打浆条件：针叶木浆在上述五个转数下依次对应 16、20、40、63、79 °SR[4]；其中“8000 转≈40 °SR”是由该有序列表位置推得（按顺序对应），文中未逐项明写。

如需具体数值，请提供 Polymers 2020, 12, 2912 的 Supplementary（s1）中 Table S1，我可据此核对并解释。

Efect of PFI Refining on H-Bonding Energies, H-Bonding Distances, and Content of H-Bonds [原文] On the whole, the amount of the O(6)H· · · O(30) H-bonds for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers decreased by 16.54% and 5.91% altogether, respectively. The decrease might be due to the cleavage among cellulose molecular chains under the mechanical action of PFI refining, which was closely related to internal and external fibrillation (as seen in Section 3.1). On the other hand, the increase illustrates that there was not only the breakage, but also the formation of O(6)H· · · O(30) H-bonds. Both the fewer inter-molecular H-bonds and the lower CI (as Section 3.2 shows) will further improve the flexibility of cellulosic fibers, due to the higher mobility of molecular chains, the accessibility, and the WRV of fibers (as seen in Section 3.1). Overall, the trend was similar to that of hardwood fibers, which first increased and then had a decrease, followed by a growth. During the whole refining, the amount of $\mathrm { O } ( 3 ) \mathrm { H } \cdots \mathrm { O } ( 5 )$ H-bonds for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers showed an upward tendency and increased by 22.78% and 8.8%, respectively. The increase might be because the stable O(3)H· · · O(5) H-bonds might have not only less breakage under the action of water as destructor to the crystallites [30], but also creation in the amorphous region upon drying. Because hydrogen bond–covalent bond synergies play an important role in the cellulose stifness axial modulus, more O(3)H· · · O(5) H-bonds will enhance the cellulose stifness [33,34]. Commercial bleached softwood and hardwood kraft pulp fibers were obtained from Zhongzhirenhe Company (Jinan, Shandong Province, China). Two pulp were treated with a PFI refiner (Hamjern Maskin A/S, Hamar, Norway) according to Tappi T248 wd-97, with a pulp consistency of 10%, the gap between the opposite refining plates was 0.2 mm, and forces per bar length were 3.33 N/mm and 1.77 N/mm for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers, respectively. The drainability was characterized by the Schopper Riegler number (SR-number) with the standards ISO 5267-1. Two pulp fibers were separately refined in a PFI refiner at 0, 4000, 8000, 12,000, and 16,000 revolutions and at 0, 4000, 8000, 12,000, and 16,000 revolutions, respectively. Corresponding various pulps with an increasing beating degree, such as 16, 20, 40, 63, and 79<sup>◦</sup> SR, were obtained for softwood fibers and 0, 26, 40, 57, and 70<sup>◦</sup> SR were obtained for hardwood fibers.

[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 2. Methods > 2.1. PFI Refining
[原文]
Commercial bleached softwood and hardwood kraft pulp fibers were obtained from Zhongzhirenhe Company (Jinan, Shandong Province, China). Two pulp were treated with a PFI refiner (Hamjern Maskin A/S, Hamar, Norway) according to Tappi T248 wd-97, with a pulp consistency of 10%, the gap between the opposite refining plates was 0.2 mm, and forces per bar length were 3.33 N/mm and 1.77 N/mm for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers, respectively. The drainability was characterized by the Schopper Riegler number (SR-number) with the standards ISO 5267-1. Two pulp fibers were separately refined in a PFI refiner at 0, 4000, 8000, 12,000, and 16,000 revolutions and at 0, 4000, 8000, 12,000, and 16,000 revolutions, respectively. Corresponding various pulps with an increasing beating degree, such as 16, 20, 40, 63, and 79<sup>◦</sup> SR, were obtained for softwood fibers and 0, 26, 40, 57, and 70<sup>◦</sup> SR were obtained for hardwood fibers.

**结论：现有可获取的正文证据中没有针叶木浆 8000 转时的 BET 比表面积具体数值。**

据所检索到的研究（商业漂白针叶木硫酸盐浆，PFI 打浆，浆浓 10%，打浆转数为 0、4000、8000、12000、16000 转）[4]，BET 比表面积等孔隙数据的实测结果列于**在线补充材料 Table S1**（“Cumulative pore volume, average pore size and specific surface area of softwood pulp fiber through refining”）[1]，正文未给出任何 m²/g 数值。正文只作定性表述：外部细纤维化随打浆增强，“与比表面积的增加一致（见 Online Resource 表 S1）”[10]；作者并将此归因于更高程度的细纤维化产生新表面和更多孔隙（同见表 S1）[10]——这是作者的机理解释，且为与形态学结果的定性对应关系，并非本文正文数据可直接验证的因果或定量关系。

因此：
- **8000 转的 BET 比表面积具体值须查该文补充材料 Table S1**，该补充材料不在当前可获取的证据范围内，无法给出数值，也不应推测。
- 可支持的仅是方向性表述：该文称比表面积随打浆而增加[10]；这属于文献的定性陈述，正文未给出逐点数值，故无法据此判断各转数间是否严格单调或增幅大小，也不能给出不确定度。
- 附带可核对的打浆条件：针叶木浆在上述五个转数下依次对应 16、20、40、63、79 °SR[4]；其中“8000 转≈40 °SR”是由该有序列表位置推得（按顺序对应），文中未逐项明写。
如需具体数值，请提供 Polymers 2020, 12, 2912 的 Supplementary（s1）中 Table S1，我可据此核对并解释。

In the first refining stage, the decrease of the CI showed that mechanical treatment may mainly act in the crystalline region. Subsequently, the growth of the CI could be interpreted as greater force acting on the amorphous region in which cocrystallization might occur upon drying under the mechanical and thermal action of PFI refining. Efect of PFI Refining on H-Bonding Energies, H-Bonding Distances, and Content of H-Bonds [原文] On the whole, the amount of the O(6)H· · · O(30) H-bonds for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers decreased by 16.54% and 5.91% altogether, respectively. The decrease might be due to the cleavage among cellulose molecular chains under the mechanical action of PFI refining, which was closely related to internal and external fibrillation (as seen in Section 3.1). On the other hand, the increase illustrates that there was not only the breakage, but also the formation of O(6)H· · · O(30) H-bonds. Both the fewer inter-molecular H-bonds and the lower CI (as Section 3.2 shows) will further improve the flexibility of cellulosic fibers, due to the higher mobility of molecular chains, the accessibility, and the WRV of fibers (as seen in Section 3.1). Overall, the trend was similar to that of hardwood fibers, which first increased and then had a decrease, followed by a growth. During the whole refining, the amount of $\mathrm { O } ( 3 ) \mathrm { H } \cdots \mathrm { O } ( 5 )$ H-bonds for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers showed an upward tendency and increased by 22.78% and 8.8%, respectively. The increase might be because the stable O(3)H· · · O(5) H-bonds might have not only less breakage under the action of water as destructor to the crystallites [30], but also creation in the amorphous region upon drying. Because hydrogen bond–covalent bond synergies play an important role in the cellulose stifness axial modulus, more O(3)H· · · O(5) H-bonds will enhance the cellulose stifness [33,34]. As to the free OH(2) and OH(6) of softwood fiber, the relative content showed a slight increase trend in general. The enhancement of the free OH(2) and OH(6) was understandable, because there was the breakage of H-bonds among cellulosic molecules, which resulted in more extensive delamination and higher specific surface area (as shown in Figure S4 and Table S1 in Online Resource). This made cellulose more accessible to water and chemicals. However, for the free OH(2) and OH(6) of hardwood fiber, the number of the free OH(2) and OH(6) decreased by 21.65% from 14.32% to 11.22%, with revolutions increasing from 0 r to 4000 r, followed by an increase of 45.37% in the stage of refining from 4000 r to 12,000 r, along with an decrease of 17.11%. It could be explained by the instability of free OH groups, which makes it easy to form new H-bonds, such as O(2)H· · · O(6) or O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>)H-bonds. Thus although there is the formation of free OH(2) and OH(6) during fibrillation, the content of the free OH(2) and OH(6) might disease; meanwhile, the content of the O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>) or the O(2)H· · · O(6) H-bonds might increase upon drying.

[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 2. Methods > 2.1. PFI Refining
[原文]
Commercial bleached softwood and hardwood kraft pulp fibers were obtained from Zhongzhirenhe Company (Jinan, Shandong Province, China). Two pulp were treated with a PFI refiner (Hamjern Maskin A/S, Hamar, Norway) according to Tappi T248 wd-97, with a pulp consistency of 10%, the gap between the opposite refining plates was 0.2 mm, and forces per bar length were 3.33 N/mm and 1.77 N/mm for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers, respectively. The drainability was characterized by the Schopper Riegler number (SR-number) with the standards ISO 5267-1. Two pulp fibers were separately refined in a PFI refiner at 0, 4000, 8000, 12,000, and 16,000 revolutions and at 0, 4000, 8000, 12,000, and 16,000 revolutions, respectively. Corresponding various pulps with an increasing beating degree, such as 16, 20, 40, 63, and 79<sup>◦</sup> SR, were obtained for softwood fibers and 0, 26, 40, 57, and 70<sup>◦</sup> SR were obtained for hardwood fibers.

The trends of CI (CI-XI and CI-XA) for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers were all similar, decreasing first and then increasing, along with a decline, as shown in Figure 4. The fluctuation of the CI was probably because of the mechanical action of PFI refining on the diferent regions of cellulose. In the first refining stage, the decrease of the CI showed that mechanical treatment may mainly act in the crystalline region. Subsequently, the growth of the CI could be interpreted as greater force acting on the amorphous region in which cocrystallization might occur upon drying under the mechanical and thermal action of PFI refining. The subsequent decrease might be the continuous destruction of crystalline region.

[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 2. Methods > 2.1. PFI Refining
[原文]
Commercial bleached softwood and hardwood kraft pulp fibers were obtained from Zhongzhirenhe Company (Jinan, Shandong Province, China). Two pulp were treated with a PFI refiner (Hamjern Maskin A/S, Hamar, Norway) according to Tappi T248 wd-97, with a pulp consistency of 10%, the gap between the opposite refining plates was 0.2 mm, and forces per bar length were 3.33 N/mm and 1.77 N/mm for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers, respectively. The drainability was characterized by the Schopper Riegler number (SR-number) with the standards ISO 5267-1. Two pulp fibers were separately refined in a PFI refiner at 0, 4000, 8000, 12,000, and 16,000 revolutions and at 0, 4000, 8000, 12,000, and 16,000 revolutions, respectively. Corresponding various pulps with an increasing beating degree, such as 16, 20, 40, 63, and 79<sup>◦</sup> SR, were obtained for softwood fibers and 0, 26, 40, 57, and 70<sup>◦</sup> SR were obtained for hardwood fibers.

candidate.answer:
**Corrected answer (review of the draft against the supplied evidence)**

**Conclusion on dry-sheet tensile performance.** For commercial bleached softwood and hardwood kraft pulps refined in a PFI mill [9], the authors state that PFI refining improved the extent of fibrillation (especially internal fibrillation) and fiber swelling, and increased the tensile strength of the sheets, without a decrease in fiber strength, as indicated by the zero-span tensile index [7]. The authors attribute the increase in tensile strength mainly to the increased fibrillation and the fines generated during PFI refining [7]. Note that this paper offers no direct evidence that “fiber strength did not contribute”; zero-span tensile only indicates that fiber strength was not reduced, and the paper does not quantify the relative contributions of bonding and fiber strength.

**Conditions.** Dry-sheet tensile was tested per TAPPI T494; wet-web strength per GB/T 12914-2008; zero-span tensile per ISO 15361 [1]. Refining: 0, 4000, 8000, 12,000 and 16,000 revolutions, 10% consistency, 0.2 mm plate gap, refining force 3.33 N/mm (softwood) and 1.77 N/mm (hardwood), giving about 16–79 °SR (softwood) and 0–70 °SR (hardwood) [9].

**Limits on the tensile numbers.** Tensile index values appear only graphically in Figure 3, panels (a) softwood and (b) hardwood [2]. That figure was not viewed, so no numeric tensile index can be quoted here, and the claim that both pulp types “increased at every refining level” (monotonic increase) is not supported by the retrieved text; the text only states a general improvement. No standard deviation, error bars, or per-species significance test is reported in the retrieved text.

**Burst index and tear index.** In the retrieved methods, results and tables, I found no test method or data for burst index or tear index; the sheet-strength tests described are only dry tensile, wet-web strength and zero-span tensile [1]. I therefore cannot provide exact burst or tear index values for the same samples: this paper does not report them. Because the search was based on retrieved chunks rather than a page-by-page check, the correct statement is “not reported in the retrieved content”, not an absolute claim that these tests were never performed.

Commercial bleached softwood and hardwood kraft pulp fibers were obtained from Zhongzhirenhe Company (Jinan, Shandong Province, China). Two pulp were treated with a PFI refiner (Hamjern Maskin A/S, Hamar, Norway) according to Tappi T248 wd-97, with a pulp consistency of 10%, the gap between the opposite refining plates was 0.2 mm, and forces per bar length were 3.33 N/mm and 1.77 N/mm for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers, respectively. The drainability was characterized by the Schopper Riegler number (SR-number) with the standards ISO 5267-1. Two pulp fibers were separately refined in a PFI refiner at 0, 4000, 8000, 12,000, and 16,000 revolutions and at 0, 4000, 8000, 12,000, and 16,000 revolutions, respectively. Corresponding various pulps with an increasing beating degree, such as 16, 20, 40, 63, and 79<sup>◦</sup> SR, were obtained for softwood fibers and 0, 26, 40, 57, and 70<sup>◦</sup> SR were obtained for hardwood fibers.

sources.text:
[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 2. Methods > 2.1. PFI Refining
[原文]
Commercial bleached softwood and hardwood kraft pulp fibers were obtained from Zhongzhirenhe Company (Jinan, Shandong Province, China). Two pulp were treated with a PFI refiner (Hamjern Maskin A/S, Hamar, Norway) according to Tappi T248 wd-97, with a pulp consistency of 10%, the gap between the opposite refining plates was 0.2 mm, and forces per bar length were 3.33 N/mm and 1.77 N/mm for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers, respectively. The drainability was characterized by the Schopper Riegler number (SR-number) with the standards ISO 5267-1. Two pulp fibers were separately refined in a PFI refiner at 0, 4000, 8000, 12,000, and 16,000 revolutions and at 0, 4000, 8000, 12,000, and 16,000 revolutions, respectively. Corresponding various pulps with an increasing beating degree, such as 16, 20, 40, 63, and 79<sup>◦</sup> SR, were obtained for softwood fibers and 0, 26, 40, 57, and 70<sup>◦</sup> SR were obtained for hardwood fibers.

claims.text:
**Corrected answer (review of the draft against the supplied evidence)**

**Conclusion on dry-sheet tensile performance.** For commercial bleached softwood and hardwood kraft pulps refined in a PFI mill [9], the authors state that PFI refining improved the extent of fibrillation (especially internal fibrillation) and fiber swelling, and increased the tensile strength of the sheets, without a decrease in fiber strength, as indicated by the zero-span tensile index [7]. The authors attribute the increase in tensile strength mainly to the increased fibrillation and the fines generated during PFI refining [7]. Note that this paper offers no direct evidence that “fiber strength did not contribute”; zero-span tensile only indicates that fiber strength was not reduced, and the paper does not quantify the relative contributions of bonding and fiber strength.

**Conditions.** Dry-sheet tensile was tested per TAPPI T494; wet-web strength per GB/T 12914-2008; zero-span tensile per ISO 15361 [1]. ## 结论：目前不能完成这两篇论文的对比

**关键缺口（未解决）**：本库中检索到的论文只有 PFI 打浆这一篇（Li 等，2020，*Polymers* 12:2912）[6]。我对《Non-Wood Fibers: Relationships of Fiber Properties with Pulp Properties》先后做了 3 次检索（用题名、非木材纤维、纤维性质与纸浆性质关系等关键词），每次检索返回的都是同一篇 PFI 论文，始终没有该文献的正文、表格或数据。因此，我无法核对它的“全部实验数据”，也无法据此给出可靠的“共同结论”；如果给出，这种结论只能是猜测。此外，两篇论文所用的原料类别不同（前者为漂白木材硫酸盐浆加 PFI 机械处理 [2]），是否具有可比前提也尚未确认。

### 已获证据：PFI 论文的结论（可留作日后比对）

1. **材料与处理条件**：漂白硫酸盐**针叶木和阔叶木**浆；PFI 打浆量设为 0、4000、8000、12000、16000 转；浆浓 10%，磨盘间隙 0.2 mm，每单位刀长作用力分别为针叶木 3.33 N/mm、阔叶木 1.77 N/mm（TAPPI T248 wd-97）；打浆度分别升至 79 °SR（针叶木，起点 16 °SR）和 70 °SR（阔叶木，起点 0 °SR）[2]。
2. **形态**：原报道称，针叶木的宏观纤丝化指数与纤维长度“变化显著”、细小纤维含量上升；阔叶木这两个参数“无显著变化”；原文用“*might be because of the lower refining pressure*”（可能因为打浆压力较低）来解释，这只是**推测，未经检验**[5][14]。打浆度和保水值（WRV）随打浆显著上升，并与比表面积、孔隙增加相一致 [5]。
3. **强度**：抗张指数随打浆上升，原文主要将其归因于纤丝化与细小纤维增加；零距抗张指数显示 **PFI 打浆未降低纤维强度** [5]。上述归因为作者的判断，对比图（Figure 3）中未读取像素数值，只依据正文陈述。
4. **结晶结构（表 1 逐点数值）**：晶型不变；CI-XI 和 CI-XA 总体先降后升再降；针叶木 CI-XI 降 4.66%、CI-XA 降 15.47%，阔叶木分别降 2.65% 和 19.4%；垂直于 (200) 晶面的微晶尺寸略增（针叶木 4.5→4.7 nm，阔叶木 4.5→4.7 nm），而 (110)、(1̄10) 面波动较大 [11][12]。
5. **相关性**：CI-XI 与分子间 O(6)H···O(3)′ 氢键含量显著正相关，Pearson r = 0.888（针叶木）、0.889（阔叶木），p < 0.05 [6][3]。注意：该系数基于每种纤维仅 5 个打浆水平，属于**相关而非因果**；现有文字未给出重复次数与误差范围。
6. **总体论断的限定**：原文称微晶尺寸、结晶度与各类氢键含量“总体变化不大”，并**假设**（“It is assumed”）PFI 是“对上位结构破坏相对较小的优良纤丝化机械处理” [3]。此处应视为作者的解释性论断：同文自身的结晶度降幅（最高约 19%）与微晶尺寸波动，与“变化不大”这一措辞存在张力；另外，该处理被称为“温和”的依据是晶型未变 [11]，而不是统计检验。

### 说明（证据覆盖范围）
- 我只阅读和引用了正文、结论与表 1 的文字；**Figure 1–3 的像素数据没有查看**，因此上述形态、强度结论均取自正文陈述，不是从图中读出的数值。
- 要完成两篇对比，仍需：第二篇的非木材原料与制浆条件、全部纤维性质（长度、宽度、粗度、壁厚、卷曲、细小纤维、化学组分）与纸浆性质（抗张、撕裂、耐破、松厚度等）数据表，以及其统计处理方法；这些均未获得。

[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction
[原文]
Mechanical, chemical, and biological treatments are usually adopted to obtain the desired physical and mechanical properties and for further utilization of the natural cellulosic fibers. Therein, Papirindustriens forskningsinstitut (PFI) refining is the most common laboratory refiner in order to improve the inter-fiber bonding capacity [1] and accessibility [2,3], and manufacture the micro-fibrillated or nano-fibrillated cellulose [4–6]. The main efects of PFI refining on fibers are: (i) internal fibrillation—delaminating, loosening, and swelling of fiber wall; (ii) external fibrillation—peeling of fibrils from the fiber surface while remaining attached; (iii) fiber shortening—fiber cutting due to shearing action, and (iv) fines formation—primary fines come from ray cells and parenchyma cells and microfibrils that are caused by fiber shortening or external fibrillation. Moreover, the PFI refining could be adopted to obtain a higher internal fibrillation than other laboratory refiners [1]. These efects of the PFI refining on cellulosic fibers will improve the accessibility, the swelling, the flexibility, and the inter-fiber bonding capacity of fibers.

[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction
[原文]
 It is assumed that these changes in the macro-level structure and properties are related to the changes of crystallinity and H-bonding network during refining [7,8].

There are some diferent conclusions regarding to the efects of PFI refining on crystallinity of cellulose, not like that of ball milling, which efectively reduces the crystallinity as the treatment progresses. Although some researchers considered that the crystallinity decreased during PFI refining for corn stover [9] or softwood pulp [10], some researchers reported that the crystallinity increased first and then decreased with the degree of refining for hardwood bleached kraft pulp fibers [11] or for unbleached eucalyptus fibers [12]. Moreover, Zhao et al. [7] reported that the crystallinity initially fluctuated upward and then downward, followed by a repeating fluctuation with PFI refining for tobacco stem mechanical pulp. None of the previous studies identified a clear trend, but the results were that the crystallinity varied during PFI refinement. Based on the large proportion of H-bonds in crystalline region of cellulose, it can be assumed that the H-bonding network might change during PFI refining.

[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction
[原文]
Fourier transformation infrared spectroscopy (FT-IR), which is sensitive to molecular structure, can be as an indirect measurement for studying H-bonding network. FT-IR deconvolution of hydroxyl groups band was adopted in order to study the changes of the energy of H-bonds and the H-bonding distance during delignification [13] or the deconstruction of cellulose [14]. Moreover, it was used to study the diferences of the content of H-bonds not only between dislocation region and normal region [15], but also among plant species [16,17]. Regarding the changes of H-bonding network during PFI refining, Yuan et al. [18] reported that the content of H-bonds and crystallinity index (CI) of eucalyptus fibers changed with the increment of beating time. Subsequently, Zhao et al. [8] found that the H-bonding energy for O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>) inter-molecular H-bonds decreased by 12.9% and evolutions of the content of certain H-bonds difered at various refining stages.

[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction
[原文]
There is still a lack of literature on the efects of PFI refinement on the H-bonding network. Particularly, the relationship between the content of H-bonds and crystallinity is still worthy of further study, which will deepen the understanding of the molecular aggregation and distribution of H-bonds, providing a molecular-scale explanation for the variations in accessibility, swelling, flexibility, and fibrillation of cellulosic fibers during PFI refinement. Therefore, this work explored the efects of PFI refinement on the CI, crystallite size, energy of H-bonds, H-bonding distance, and content of H-bonds for softwood pulp fibers and hardwood pulp fibers. Attempts were made in order to establish the correlations between the CI and content of various H-bonds.

[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 2. Methods > 2.1. PFI Refining
[原文]
Commercial bleached softwood and hardwood kraft pulp fibers were obtained from Zhongzhirenhe Company (Jinan, Shandong Province, China). Two pulp were treated with a PFI refiner (Hamjern Maskin A/S, Hamar, Norway) according to Tappi T248 wd-97, with a pulp consistency of 10%, the gap between the opposite refining plates was 0.2 mm, and forces per bar length were 3.33 N/mm and 1.77 N/mm for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers, respectively. The drainability was characterized by the Schopper Riegler number (SR-number) with the standards ISO 5267-1. Two pulp fibers were separately refined in a PFI refiner at 0, 4000, 8000, 12,000, and 16,000 revolutions and at 0, 4000, 8000, 12,000, and 16,000 revolutions, respectively. Corresponding various pulps with an increasing beating degree, such as 16, 20, 40, 63, and 79<sup>◦</sup> SR, were obtained for softwood fibers and 0, 26, 40, 57, and 70<sup>◦</sup> SR were obtained for hardwood fibers.

[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 4. Conclusions
[原文]
upramolecular structure, including crystallite size, crystallinity, and content of various H-bonds.PFI refining acts not only on the macro-level structure and mechanical properties, but also on The results indicated that the fibrillation and properties of fibers are related to the variation of thethe supramolecular structure, including crystallite size, crystallinity, and content of various H-bonds.

[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 4. Conclusions
[原文]
The results indicated that the fibrillation and properties of fibers are related to the variation of the supramolecular structure during PFI refining. It is noticeable that there was a significantly positive correlation between the CI-XI and content of O(6)H· · · O(3)’ H-bonds during PFI refining for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers. Thus, the trend of the content of O(6)H· · · O(3)’ H-bonds might be generally speculated based on CI-XI while refining. Besides, the crystallite size, crystallinity, and content of various H-bonds did not change much in general. It is assumed that PFI refining is an excellent mechanical treatment of fibrillation with relatively little destruction on the supramolecular structure.

Abstract: Supramolecular structure is the critical factor that afects the properties of cellulosic fibers. This article studied the action of Papirindustriens forskningsinstitut (PFI) refining on the molecular aggregation and hydrogen bonding network, and tried to explore the relationship between the crystal packing and hydrogen-bonding network in cellulosic fibers. The results showed that the polymorph, H-bonding distance, and H-bonding energy of various H-bonds remained almost unchanged, while the crystalline index, crystallite size, and content of various H-bonds changed with refining. Therein, the content of the inter-molecular O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>) H-bonds was significantly correlated with the crystalline index that was obtained in intensities of the XRD peaks. The Pearson correlation coeficient between them was 0.888 (p < 0.05) for softwood fibers and 0.889 (p < 0.05) for hardwood fibers, respectively. It can be concluded that the variations of accessibility, swelling, and fibrillation were closely related to the supramolecular structure and the intermolecular H-bonds play an important role in the crystal packing of cellulose.

[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction
[原文]
 It is assumed that these changes in the macro-level structure and properties are related to the changes of crystallinity and H-bonding network during refining [7,8].

There are some diferent conclusions regarding to the efects of PFI refining on crystallinity of cellulose, not like that of ball milling, which efectively reduces the crystallinity as the treatment progresses. Although some researchers considered that the crystallinity decreased during PFI refining for corn stover [9] or softwood pulp [10], some researchers reported that the crystallinity increased first and then decreased with the degree of refining for hardwood bleached kraft pulp fibers [11] or for unbleached eucalyptus fibers [12]. Moreover, Zhao et al. [7] reported that the crystallinity initially fluctuated upward and then downward, followed by a repeating fluctuation with PFI refining for tobacco stem mechanical pulp. None of the previous studies identified a clear trend, but the results were that the crystallinity varied during PFI refinement. Based on the large proportion of H-bonds in crystalline region of cellulose, it can be assumed that the H-bonding network might change during PFI refining.

[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction
[原文]
Fourier transformation infrared spectroscopy (FT-IR), which is sensitive to molecular structure, can be as an indirect measurement for studying H-bonding network. FT-IR deconvolution of hydroxyl groups band was adopted in order to study the changes of the energy of H-bonds and the H-bonding distance during delignification [13] or the deconstruction of cellulose [14]. Moreover, it was used to study the diferences of the content of H-bonds not only between dislocation region and normal region [15], but also among plant species [16,17]. Regarding the changes of H-bonding network during PFI refining, Yuan et al. [18] reported that the content of H-bonds and crystallinity index (CI) of eucalyptus fibers changed with the increment of beating time. Subsequently, Zhao et al. [8] found that the H-bonding energy for O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>) inter-molecular H-bonds decreased by 12.9% and evolutions of the content of certain H-bonds difered at various refining stages.

[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction
[原文]
There is still a lack of literature on the efects of PFI refinement on the H-bonding network. Particularly, the relationship between the content of H-bonds and crystallinity is still worthy of further study, which will deepen the understanding of the molecular aggregation and distribution of H-bonds, providing a molecular-scale explanation for the variations in accessibility, swelling, flexibility, and fibrillation of cellulosic fibers during PFI refinement. Therefore, this work explored the efects of PFI refinement on the CI, crystallite size, energy of H-bonds, H-bonding distance, and content of H-bonds for softwood pulp fibers and hardwood pulp fibers. Attempts were made in order to establish the correlations between the CI and content of various H-bonds.

[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 2. Methods > 2.1. PFI Refining
[原文]
Commercial bleached softwood and hardwood kraft pulp fibers were obtained from Zhongzhirenhe Company (Jinan, Shandong Province, China). Two pulp were treated with a PFI refiner (Hamjern Maskin A/S, Hamar, Norway) according to Tappi T248 wd-97, with a pulp consistency of 10%, the gap between the opposite refining plates was 0.2 mm, and forces per bar length were 3.33 N/mm and 1.77 N/mm for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers, respectively. The drainability was characterized by the Schopper Riegler number (SR-number) with the standards ISO 5267-1. Two pulp fibers were separately refined in a PFI refiner at 0, 4000, 8000, 12,000, and 16,000 revolutions and at 0, 4000, 8000, 12,000, and 16,000 revolutions, respectively. Corresponding various pulps with an increasing beating degree, such as 16, 20, 40, 63, and 79<sup>◦</sup> SR, were obtained for softwood fibers and 0, 26, 40, 57, and 70<sup>◦</sup> SR were obtained for hardwood fibers.

[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 4. Conclusions
[原文]
The results indicated that the fibrillation and properties of fibers are related to the variation of the supramolecular structure during PFI refining. It is noticeable that there was a significantly positive correlation between the CI-XI and content of O(6)H· · · O(3)’ H-bonds during PFI refining for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers. Thus, the trend of the content of O(6)H· · · O(3)’ H-bonds might be generally speculated based on CI-XI while refining. Besides, the crystallite size, crystallinity, and content of various H-bonds did not change much in general. It is assumed that PFI refining is an excellent mechanical treatment of fibrillation with relatively little destruction on the supramolecular structure.

Abstract: Supramolecular structure is the critical factor that afects the properties of cellulosic fibers. This article studied the action of Papirindustriens forskningsinstitut (PFI) refining on the molecular aggregation and hydrogen bonding network, and tried to explore the relationship between the crystal packing and hydrogen-bonding network in cellulosic fibers. The results showed that the polymorph, H-bonding distance, and H-bonding energy of various H-bonds remained almost unchanged, while the crystalline index, crystallite size, and content of various H-bonds changed with refining. Therein, the content of the inter-molecular O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>) H-bonds was significantly correlated with the crystalline index that was obtained in intensities of the XRD peaks. The Pearson correlation coeficient between them was 0.888 (p < 0.05) for softwood fibers and 0.889 (p < 0.05) for hardwood fibers, respectively. It can be concluded that the variations of accessibility, swelling, and fibrillation were closely related to the supramolecular structure and the intermolecular H-bonds play an important role in the crystal packing of cellulose.

## 结论：目前不能完成这两篇论文的对比

**关键缺口（未解决）**：本库中检索到的论文只有 PFI 打浆这一篇（Li 等，2020，*Polymers* 12:2912）[6]。我对《Non-Wood Fibers: Relationships of Fiber Properties with Pulp Properties》先后做了 3 次检索（用题名、非木材纤维、纤维性质与纸浆性质关系等关键词），每次检索返回的都是同一篇 PFI 论文，始终没有该文献的正文、表格或数据。因此，我无法核对它的“全部实验数据”，也无法据此给出可靠的“共同结论”；如果给出，这种结论只能是猜测。此外，两篇论文所用的原料类别不同（前者为漂白木材硫酸盐浆加 PFI 机械处理 [2]），是否具有可比前提也尚未确认。

### 已获证据：PFI 论文的结论（可留作日后比对）

1. **材料与处理条件**：漂白硫酸盐**针叶木和阔叶木**浆；PFI 打浆量设为 0、4000、8000、12000、16000 转；浆浓 10%，磨盘间隙 0.2 mm，每单位刀长作用力分别为针叶木 3.33 N/mm、阔叶木 1.77 N/mm（TAPPI T248 wd-97）；打浆度分别升至 79 °SR（针叶木，起点 16 °SR）和 70 °SR（阔叶木，起点 0 °SR）[2]。
2. **形态**：原报道称，针叶木的宏观纤丝化指数与纤维长度“变化显著”、细小纤维含量上升；阔叶木这两个参数“无显著变化”；原文用“*might be because of the lower refining pressure*”（可能因为打浆压力较低）来解释，这只是**推测，未经检验**[5][14]。打浆度和保水值（WRV）随打浆显著上升，并与比表面积、孔隙增加相一致 [5]。
3. **强度**：抗张指数随打浆上升，原文主要将其归因于纤丝化与细小纤维增加；零距抗张指数显示 **PFI 打浆未降低纤维强度** [5]。上述归因为作者的判断，对比图（Figure 3）中未读取像素数值，只依据正文陈述。
4. **结晶结构（表 1 逐点数值）**：晶型不变；CI-XI 和 CI-XA 总体先降后升再降；针叶木 CI-XI 降 4.66%、CI-XA 降 15.47%，阔叶木分别降 2.65% 和 19.4%；垂直于 (200) 晶面的微晶尺寸略增（针叶木 4.5→4.7 nm，阔叶木 4.5→4.7 nm），而 (110)、(1̄10) 面波动较大 [11][12]。
5. **相关性**：CI-XI 与分子间 O(6)H···O(3)′ 氢键含量显著正相关，Pearson r = 0.888（针叶木）、0.889（阔叶木），p < 0.05 [6][3]。注意：该系数基于每种纤维仅 5 个打浆水平，属于**相关而非因果**；现有文字未给出重复次数与误差范围。
6. **总体论断的限定**：原文称微晶尺寸、结晶度与各类氢键含量“总体变化不大”，并**假设**（“It is assumed”）PFI 是“对上位结构破坏相对较小的优良纤丝化机械处理” [3]。此处应视为作者的解释性论断：同文自身的结晶度降幅（最高约 19%）与微晶尺寸波动，与“变化不大”这一措辞存在张力；另外，该处理被称为“温和”的依据是晶型未变 [11]，而不是统计检验。

### 说明（证据覆盖范围）
- 我只阅读和引用了正文、结论与表 1 的文字；**Figure 1–3 的像素数据没有查看**，因此上述形态、强度结论均取自正文陈述，不是从图中读出的数值。
- 要完成两篇对比，仍需：第二篇的非木材原料与制浆条件、全部纤维性质（长度、宽度、粗度、壁厚、卷曲、细小纤维、化学组分）与纸浆性质（抗张、撕裂、耐破、松厚度等）数据表，以及其统计处理方法；这些均未获得。

4. **结晶结构（表 1 逐点数值）**：晶型不变；CI-XI 和 CI-XA 总体先降后升再降；针叶木 CI-XI 降 4.66%、CI-XA 降 15.47%，阔叶木分别降 2.65% 和 19.4%；垂直于 (200) 晶面的微晶尺寸略增（针叶木 4.5→4.7 nm，阔叶木 4.5→4.7 nm），而 (110)、(1̄10) 面波动较大 [11][12]。
5. **相关性**：CI-XI 与分子间 O(6)H···O(3)′ 氢键含量显著正相关，Pearson r = 0.888（针叶木）、0.889（阔叶木），p < 0.05 [6][3]。注意：该系数基于每种纤维仅 5 个打浆水平，属于**相关而非因果**；现有文字未给出重复次数与误差范围。
6. **总体论断的限定**：原文称微晶尺寸、结晶度与各类氢键含量“总体变化不大”，并**假设**（“It is assumed”）PFI 是“对上位结构破坏相对较小的优良纤丝化机械处理” [3]。此处应视为作者的解释性论断：同文自身的结晶度降幅（最高约 19%）与微晶尺寸波动，与“变化不大”这一措辞存在张力；另外，该处理被称为“温和”的依据是晶型未变 [11]，而不是统计检验。

### 说明（证据覆盖范围）
- 我只阅读和引用了正文、结论与表 1 的文字；**Figure 1–3 的像素数据没有查看**，因此上述形态、强度结论均取自正文陈述，不是从图中读出的数值。
- 要完成两篇对比，仍需：第二篇的非木材原料与制浆条件、全部纤维性质（长度、宽度、粗度、壁厚、卷曲、细小纤维、化学组分）与纸浆性质（抗张、撕裂、耐破、松厚度等）数据表，以及其统计处理方法；这些均未获得。

**无法给出所问的验证集 R²、RMSE 及最佳模型名称**：已获取的证据中，不足以支持这些事实。

已获取的文献内容均来自同一篇关于 PFI 精磨对纤维素聚集结构影响的论文 [1][2][3][4]，并非纸张抗张强度的机器学习预测研究：

- 该文将抗张强度作为精磨过程的实验测试指标；文中提到，在 PFI 精磨过程中，抗张指数、零-span 抗张指数和湿纸幅强度随精磨转数变化，抗张强度增加主要与纤维分丝帚化和细小纤维有关，[1]。
- 抗张强度检测方法见 [2]，但其中未涉及训练集/验证集划分、预测模型比较或模型性能评价。
- 文中出现的 r²=0.9989–0.9996 是 FT‑IR 羟基谱带分峰非线性拟合的决定系数，[3]，**不是**预测模型验证集的 R²，不能据此推断模型性能。
- 在已获取的段落和表格中，未发现 RMSE、验证集 R²、最佳模型名称，也未发现“已训练好的纸张抗张预测模型”这一对象。

因此，**验证集 R²、RMSE 和最佳模型名称均为未解决的信息缺口**。需提供该预测模型论文的题名、DOI 或相关结果表，才能准确回答；也不应将上述 FT‑IR 拟合 r² 误作验证集 R²。

The fines content, weighted mean length, and macro-fibrillation index of each sample were determined with a MORFI LB analyzer (Techpap SAS, Grenoble, France). The tensile strength of dry sheets and Wet-web strength were tested according to TAPPI T494 and Chinese standard GBT 12914-2008, respectively. The zero-span tensile strength was tested with the Z-Span 2400 apparatus (Pulmac International Co. Ltd., Montpelier, VT, USA), according to the standard ISO 15361.

candidate.answer:
## 结论：检索到的文献证据与“阔叶木增幅更大”的前提相反

本次检索到的语料中，只有 Li 2020（PFI 打浆，0–16,000 转）直接对比了针叶木与阔叶木浆的湿纸幅强度，其结论是：针叶木湿纸幅强度增幅更显著，阔叶木增幅较小 [1]。原文表述为“softwood fiber had a more significant increase when compared to that of hardwood fiber” [1]。该结论为定性描述，文中未给出湿纸幅强度的数值、统计检验或误差范围。

**图3的目测读数（近似值，非原文引用的数值）** [6]
图3左轴为“Tensile index of wet sheet (N·m/g)”，范围 0–8，两种浆共用同一左轴；黑点为湿纸幅抗张指数。据此目测：
- 针叶木（a）：0 转约 0.8，16,000 转约 4.3–4.4，绝对增量约 3.5，约为初始值的 5 倍；
- 阔叶木（b）：0 转约 0.7，16,000 转约 1.8–1.9，绝对增量约 1.1，约为初始值的 2.5 倍。

在本次条件下，针叶木的湿纸幅强度在绝对增量和相对倍数上均大于阔叶木；此外，阔叶木在整个打浆过程中始终处于更低的强度水平 [6]。图中数据点带有误差棒，但图中未标注样本数或统计显著性；并且两浆是在相同转数下比较，并未在相同打浆能量或相同打浆度（游离度）下比较，因此这种横向比较会受打浆条件差异干扰，不能直接等同于“阔叶木对打浆的固有响应更弱”。

**作者给出的解释**
1. **纤维长度是关键**：原文明确写道“It is for that fiber length plays an essential role in wet–web strength”[1]。即湿纸幅靠纤维网络缠结承载，长纤维的搭接贡献更大。
2. **两种浆的打浆形态响应不同**：PFI 过程中，针叶木的细小纤维含量呈上升趋势，并且纤维长度与宏细纤维化（macro-fibrillation）指数变化显著；而阔叶木的宏细纤维化指数和纤维长度这两项参数“相对针叶木无显著变化”（no significant variations relative to softwood fibers）[1]。
   - 作者对此给出的**推测性**解释是：阔叶木施加的打浆压力更低（“It might be because of the lower refining pressure that was applied in hardwood fibers”）[1]。这是“might be”式推测，未做验证。
   - 需注意：原文只报告了针叶木细小纤维含量上升，并未给出阔叶木细小纤维或比表面积的对比幅度。因此，“阔叶木细纤维化/细小纤维生成更少、可增加结合面积有限”属于由上述形态数据外推的解释，不是原文陈述 [1]。
3. 零span抗张指数结果显示 PFI 未降低单纤维强度 [1]。由此推断差别更多来自网络结合与纤维长度而非单纤维被削弱，这是合理推断，但原文并未做此因果论证。

**证据缺口**
- 湿纸幅强度的具体数值、增幅百分比与统计显著性：原文未给出，只能依赖目测读图 [6]。
- 是否在等打浆度/等能量下比较：原文按等转数比较；虽然打浆度和保水值随转数上升 [1]，但未给出两浆在等打浆度下的对照。
- 若你所观察到的是其他体系（不同打浆设备或强度、高浓打浆、不同打浆度起点，或比较的是保水值、打浆度、结合面积等指标），本语料无相应数据支持，无法判断阔叶木是否确实“涨得更多”，需提供具体文献或条件再核对。

本次检索到的语料中，只有 Li 2020（PFI 打浆，0–16,000 转）直接对比了针叶木与阔叶木浆的湿纸幅强度，其结论是：针叶木湿纸幅强度增幅更显著，阔叶木增幅较小 [1]。原文表述为“softwood fiber had a more significant increase when compared to that of hardwood fiber” [1]。该结论为定性描述，文中未给出湿纸幅强度的数值、统计检验或误差范围。

**图3的目测读数（近似值，非原文引用的数值）** [6]
图3左轴为“Tensile index of wet sheet (N·m/g)”，范围 0–8，两种浆共用同一左轴；黑点为湿纸幅抗张指数。据此目测：
- 针叶木（a）：0 转约 0.8，16,000 转约 4.3–4.4，绝对增量约 3.5，约为初始值的 5 倍；
- 阔叶木（b）：0 转约 0.7，16,000 转约 1.8–1.9，绝对增量约 1.1，约为初始值的 2.5 倍。
在本次条件下，针叶木的湿纸幅强度在绝对增量和相对倍数上均大于阔叶木；此外，阔叶木在整个打浆过程中始终处于更低的强度水平 [6]。图中数据点带有误差棒，但图中未标注样本数或统计显著性；并且两浆是在相同转数下比较，并未在相同打浆能量或相同打浆度（游离度）下比较，因此这种横向比较会受打浆条件差异干扰，不能直接等同于“阔叶木对打浆的固有响应更弱”。

**作者给出的解释**
1. **纤维长度是关键**：原文明确写道“It is for that fiber length plays an essential role in wet–web strength”[1]。即湿纸幅靠纤维网络缠结承载，长纤维的搭接贡献更大。
2. **两种浆的打浆形态响应不同**：PFI 过程中，针叶木的细小纤维含量呈上升趋势，并且纤维长度与宏细纤维化（macro-fibrillation）指数变化显著；而阔叶木的宏细纤维化指数和纤维长度这两项参数“相对针叶木无显著变化”（no significant variations relative to softwood fibers）[1]。
   - 作者对此给出的**推测性**解释是：阔叶木施加的打浆压力更低（“It might be because of the lower refining pressure that was applied in hardwood fibers”）[1]。这是“might be”式推测，未做验证。
   - 需注意：原文只报告了针叶木细小纤维含量上升，并未给出阔叶木细小纤维或比表面积的对比幅度。因此，“阔叶木细纤维化/细小纤维生成更少、可增加结合面积有限”属于由上述形态数据外推的解释，不是原文陈述 [1]。
3. 零span抗张指数结果显示 PFI 未降低单纤维强度 [1]。由此推断差别更多来自网络结合与纤维长度而非单纤维被削弱，这是合理推断，但原文并未做此因果论证。

**证据缺口**
- 湿纸幅强度的具体数值、增幅百分比与统计显著性：原文未给出，只能依赖目测读图 [6]。
- 是否在等打浆度/等能量下比较：原文按等转数比较；虽然打浆度和保水值随转数上升 [1]，但未给出两浆在等打浆度下的对照。
- 若你所观察到的是其他体系（不同打浆设备或强度、高浓打浆、不同打浆度起点，或比较的是保水值、打浆度、结合面积等指标），本语料无相应数据支持，无法判断阔叶木是否确实“涨得更多”，需提供具体文献或条件再核对。

basis.text: In Figure 3, the tensile index, zero-span tensile index, and wet-web strength represented as a function of the refining revolutions. The increment of tensile strength is mainly caused by the increasing fibrillation and fines during PFI refining, as mentioned above. The wet–web strength of softwood fiber had a more significant increase when compared to that of hardwood fiber. It is for that fiber length plays an essential role in wet–web strength. The zero-span tensile index was usually used in characterizing the tensile strength of fibers. The results of the zero-span tensile index showed that PFI refining did not reduce fiber strength, which is consistent with the report of Kouko et al. [24]. The above results showed that PFI refining improved the extent of fibrillation (especially the internal fibrillation), the swelling of fibers, and the tensile strength of sheets without a decrease of the tensile strength of fibers.

candidate.answer:
## 结论（对前提的修正）

**在本次提供的文献中，并不存在“PFI 打浆使纤维素 I 型转变为 II 型”这一前提。** XRD 结果表明，针叶木浆与阔叶木浆在**整个 PFI 打浆过程中晶型均未发生变化**（原始谱图见 Online Resource 图 S1、S2）；作者据此把 PFI 打浆判断为"相对温和的机械处理" [2][7]。因此，文中讨论的结晶度下降，针对的是**仍为纤维素 I 型（按 Iβ 晶格标定）**的样品；"纤维素 II 型结晶度还下降"并不是该文的结论。

## 文中实际观测到的结晶度变化

打浆转数范围为 0、4000、8000、12000、16000 转。针叶木与阔叶木的 CI-XI（峰强法）和 CI-XA（峰面积/拟合面积法）都表现为**波动而非单调下降**：先降低，再回升，随后下降 [2][5]。

端点数值（表 1）[5]：

| 样品 | CI-XI | CI-XA |
|---|---|---|
| 针叶木 | 73.23% → 69.82% | 40.46% → 34.20% |
| 阔叶木 | 75.55% → 73.55% | 47.16% → 38.01% |

原文表述的降幅（4.66%、15.47%；2.65%、19.4%）是**相对降幅**；按表 1 数值换算，绝对降幅约为 3.4、6.3、2.0、9.2 个百分点（后者为本次换算，并非原文给出的数字）。表中中间转数点也有回升（如针叶木 CI-XI 在 8000 转回升至 72.54%），所以用端点差值描述趋势会掩盖这种波动 [5]。

## 作者给出的机理解释（原文用"可能/可解释为"等推断性措辞）

- **初期 CI 下降**：机械作用**可能**主要作用于结晶区，使晶区受到破坏；
- **随后 CI 回升**：作用力**可能**更多转向无定形区，干燥过程中在打浆的机械与热作用下**可能发生共结晶**；
- **再下降**：结晶区**可能**被持续破坏 [2]。

这些是作者提出的阶段性假设，并未通过分区定量或原位手段直接验证，因此不应表述为已确定的机制。

## 一个重要的反直觉细节：CI 下降，但 (200) 方向微晶尺寸反而增大

打浆过程中，两种浆**垂直于 (200) 晶面**的微晶尺寸呈上升趋势（表 1：针叶木 4.5→4.7 nm，阔叶木 4.5→4.7 nm）。作者将其归因于分子链并合（coalescence）或相邻微纤丝在干燥时 (200) 面取向一致的结晶学堆叠，**也可能**是因为 (200) 面较难被水分子渗透、受到的劈裂作用更弱 [5]。垂直 (110)/(1-10) 方向的尺寸波动更大，作者认为这与这些亲水晶面在准晶区间可被水分子渗入、从而承受更多机械作用（并伴随黏附/共结晶与断链）有关 [2][7]。因此，"结晶度指数下降"不能简单等同于"晶体整体变小或全部非晶化"。

## 氢键相关性的证据（相关，不等于因果）

O(6)H···O(3′) 氢键含量也呈"先降—升—再降"的变化，与 CI-XI 的 Pearson 相关系数为针叶木 **0.912**、阔叶木 **0.889**（均 p<0.05）。作者**推测**这是由于结晶区中该氢键的含量高于无定形区 [6]。该证据属于统计相关性；另外，统计时 CI-XI 与 CI-XA 本身也显著相关（0.919 / 0.925，p<0.05），所以不能据此推断"氢键变化导致结晶度变化"的因果链 [7]。

## 测量方法上的限定（以及一条未被文献支持的推断）

- CI-XI 用 Segal 式：以 2θ 22–23° 的 (200) 峰强与 18–19° 无定形最低强度计算；CI-XA 由 Savitzky–Golay 平滑、线性基线校正后用 Pearson VII 分峰，取晶峰面积占比 [8]。文中明确声明所有指标均按 **Iβ** 晶格标定（天然纤维素含 Iα/Iβ 两种多晶型）[8]。
- CI-XI 显著高于 CI-XA，作者认为**可能是** CI-XA 分析中无定形贡献被过度拟合所致 [7]。
- 微晶尺寸由 Scherrer 方程算出；因未扣除仪器展宽，计算值**可能低于**真实值 [8]。
- **以下是我的推断，并非本文内容，也未经本次证据验证**：纤维素 II 的主峰位置与 I 型不同，把基于 Iβ (200) 的指数直接用于 II 型样品，可能得到失真的"表观结晶度"。若你的资料来源确实发生了 I→II 转变，需要核对该来源的晶型判定与结晶度算法是否匹配，而不能沿用本文的数值。

## 未能解决的证据缺口

1. 本次检索到的语料中只有这一篇 PFI 相关文献，**没有任何报告"PFI 打浆导致纤维素 I→II"的原始数据**（通常 I→II 转变需碱化/丝光或溶解再生等处理）。若你指的是另一篇论文，请提供出处。
2. 已获取的证据未包含该文的浆料细节（是否漂白硫酸盐浆、打浆浓度、比压、间隙等）与误差/重复性信息，因此不能对条件与不确定度作进一步说明。
3. 未对图 4、图 5、图 8、图 9 及表 1 的图片做像素级查看，以上数值与趋势均依据正文与表 1 的文本记录 [2][5][6]，不含图像读数结论。

[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction
[原文]
Mechanical, chemical, and biological treatments are usually adopted to obtain the desired physical and mechanical properties and for further utilization of the natural cellulosic fibers. Therein, Papirindustriens forskningsinstitut (PFI) refining is the most common laboratory refiner in order to improve the inter-fiber bonding capacity [1] and accessibility [2,3], and manufacture the micro-fibrillated or nano-fibrillated cellulose [4–6]. The main efects of PFI refining on fibers are: (i) internal fibrillation—delaminating, loosening, and swelling of fiber wall; (ii) external fibrillation—peeling of fibrils from the fiber surface while remaining attached; (iii) fiber shortening—fiber cutting due to shearing action, and (iv) fines formation—primary fines come from ray cells and parenchyma cells and microfibrils that are caused by fiber shortening or external fibrillation. Moreover, the PFI refining could be adopted to obtain a higher internal fibrillation than other laboratory refiners [1]. These efects of the PFI refining on cellulosic fibers will improve the accessibility, the swelling, the flexibility, and the inter-fiber bonding capacity of fibers.

[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction
[原文]
 It is assumed that these changes in the macro-level structure and properties are related to the changes of crystallinity and H-bonding network during refining [7,8].

There are some diferent conclusions regarding to the efects of PFI refining on crystallinity of cellulose, not like that of ball milling, which efectively reduces the crystallinity as the treatment progresses. Although some researchers considered that the crystallinity decreased during PFI refining for corn stover [9] or softwood pulp [10], some researchers reported that the crystallinity increased first and then decreased with the degree of refining for hardwood bleached kraft pulp fibers [11] or for unbleached eucalyptus fibers [12]. Moreover, Zhao et al. [7] reported that the crystallinity initially fluctuated upward and then downward, followed by a repeating fluctuation with PFI refining for tobacco stem mechanical pulp. None of the previous studies identified a clear trend, but the results were that the crystallinity varied during PFI refinement. Based on the large proportion of H-bonds in crystalline region of cellulose, it can be assumed that the H-bonding network might change during PFI refining.

[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction
[原文]
Fourier transformation infrared spectroscopy (FT-IR), which is sensitive to molecular structure, can be as an indirect measurement for studying H-bonding network. FT-IR deconvolution of hydroxyl groups band was adopted in order to study the changes of the energy of H-bonds and the H-bonding distance during delignification [13] or the deconstruction of cellulose [14]. Moreover, it was used to study the diferences of the content of H-bonds not only between dislocation region and normal region [15], but also among plant species [16,17]. Regarding the changes of H-bonding network during PFI refining, Yuan et al. [18] reported that the content of H-bonds and crystallinity index (CI) of eucalyptus fibers changed with the increment of beating time. Subsequently, Zhao et al. [8] found that the H-bonding energy for O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>) inter-molecular H-bonds decreased by 12.9% and evolutions of the content of certain H-bonds difered at various refining stages.

[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction
[原文]
There is still a lack of literature on the efects of PFI refinement on the H-bonding network. Particularly, the relationship between the content of H-bonds and crystallinity is still worthy of further study, which will deepen the understanding of the molecular aggregation and distribution of H-bonds, providing a molecular-scale explanation for the variations in accessibility, swelling, flexibility, and fibrillation of cellulosic fibers during PFI refinement. Therefore, this work explored the efects of PFI refinement on the CI, crystallite size, energy of H-bonds, H-bonding distance, and content of H-bonds for softwood pulp fibers and hardwood pulp fibers. Attempts were made in order to establish the correlations between the CI and content of various H-bonds.

[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 2. Methods > 2.4. XRD Analysis
[原文]
The crystallinity of pretreated fibers was determined by a Shimadzu XRD 7000S (Shimadzu, Kyoto, Japan), while using Cu-Ka radiation. The samples were scanned at 40 kV and 30 mA in a 2θ range of $4 { - } 4 0 ^ { \circ }$ at 1<sup>◦</sup>/min. It is well known that two polymorphs, cellulose Iα and Iβ, are present in native cellulose; for clarity, all of the reflections indexed here are on the Iβ lattice. Before analysis, the experimental data is nine point smoothed with Savitzky–Golay algorithm. The two types of CI values were obtained from peak intensity method (CI − XI) and peak fitting (CI-XA), respectively. The CI − XI was calculated as in Equation (2) [19].

[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 2. Methods > 2.4. XRD Analysis
[原文]
where I200 is the maximum difraction intensity value of the (200) lattice plane between the scattering angles of $2 \Theta = 2 2 ^ { \circ }$ and $2 3 ^ { \circ }$ , and $I _ { a m }$ is the minimum difraction intensity of amorphous fraction between $2 \Theta = 1 8 ^ { \circ }$ and $1 9 ^ { \circ }$

All of the XRD difractograms were smoothed with the Savitzky–Golay algorithm and baseline-corrected with linear fit function. Subsequently, the baseline-corrected difractograms were deconvoluted with the Pearson VII function. The value of the CI-XA equals the area percentage occupied by crystalline peaks over the total area of the difraction pattern [20]. In addition, the crystallite size was calculated by the widely used Scherrer Equation (3) [21]:

[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 2. Methods > 2.4. XRD Analysis
[原文]
$$
L = \frac {k \times \lambda}{(\beta \times \cos \theta)}\tag{3}
$$

[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 2. Methods > 2.4. XRD Analysis
[原文]
where L is the size that is perpendicular to the lattice plane, k is a constant that depends on the crystal shape (0.89), λ is the wavelength of the incident beam in the difraction experiment (0.154 nm), $\beta$ is the full width at half maximum of the difraction peak, and θ is the Bragg’s angle. In general, the values of the calculated crystallite sizes might be lower than that of the real crystallite sizes, because the peak broadening from the instrumental factors was not considered [22].

## 结论（对前提的修正）

**在本次提供的文献中，并不存在“PFI 打浆使纤维素 I 型转变为 II 型”这一前提。** XRD 结果表明，针叶木浆与阔叶木浆在**整个 PFI 打浆过程中晶型均未发生变化**（原始谱图见 Online Resource 图 S1、S2）；作者据此把 PFI 打浆判断为"相对温和的机械处理" [2][7]。因此，文中讨论的结晶度下降，针对的是**仍为纤维素 I 型（按 Iβ 晶格标定）**的样品；"纤维素 II 型结晶度还下降"并不是该文的结论。

## 文中实际观测到的结晶度变化

打浆转数范围为 0、4000、8000、12000、16000 转。针叶木与阔叶木的 CI-XI（峰强法）和 CI-XA（峰面积/拟合面积法）都表现为**波动而非单调下降**：先降低，再回升，随后下降 [2][5]。
原文表述的降幅（4.66%、15.47%；2.65%、19.4%）是**相对降幅**；按表 1 数值换算，绝对降幅约为 3.4、6.3、2.0、9.2 个百分点（后者为本次换算，并非原文给出的数字）。表中中间转数点也有回升（如针叶木 CI-XI 在 8000 转回升至 72.54%），所以用端点差值描述趋势会掩盖这种波动 [5]。

## 作者给出的机理解释（原文用"可能/可解释为"等推断性措辞）

- **初期 CI 下降**：机械作用**可能**主要作用于结晶区，使晶区受到破坏；
- **随后 CI 回升**：作用力**可能**更多转向无定形区，干燥过程中在打浆的机械与热作用下**可能发生共结晶**；
- **再下降**：结晶区**可能**被持续破坏 [2]。
这些是作者提出的阶段性假设，并未通过分区定量或原位手段直接验证，因此不应表述为已确定的机制。

## 一个重要的反直觉细节：CI 下降，但 (200) 方向微晶尺寸反而增大

打浆过程中，两种浆**垂直于 (200) 晶面**的微晶尺寸呈上升趋势（表 1：针叶木 4.5→4.7 nm，阔叶木 4.5→4.7 nm）。作者将其归因于分子链并合（coalescence）或相邻微纤丝在干燥时 (200) 面取向一致的结晶学堆叠，**也可能**是因为 (200) 面较难被水分子渗透、受到的劈裂作用更弱 [5]。垂直 (110)/(1-10) 方向的尺寸波动更大，作者认为这与这些亲水晶面在准晶区间可被水分子渗入、从而承受更多机械作用（并伴随黏附/共结晶与断链）有关 [2][7]。因此，"结晶度指数下降"不能简单等同于"晶体整体变小或全部非晶化"。

## 氢键相关性的证据（相关，不等于因果）

O(6)H···O(3′) 氢键含量也呈"先降—升—再降"的变化，与 CI-XI 的 Pearson 相关系数为针叶木 **0.912**、阔叶木 **0.889**（均 p<0.05）。作者**推测**这是由于结晶区中该氢键的含量高于无定形区 [6]。该证据属于统计相关性；另外，统计时 CI-XI 与 CI-XA 本身也显著相关（0.919 / 0.925，p<0.05），所以不能据此推断"氢键变化导致结晶度变化"的因果链 [7]。

## 测量方法上的限定（以及一条未被文献支持的推断）

- CI-XI 用 Segal 式：以 2θ 22–23° 的 (200) 峰强与 18–19° 无定形最低强度计算；CI-XA 由 Savitzky–Golay 平滑、线性基线校正后用 Pearson VII 分峰，取晶峰面积占比 [8]。文中明确声明所有指标均按 **Iβ** 晶格标定（天然纤维素含 Iα/Iβ 两种多晶型）[8]。
- CI-XI 显著高于 CI-XA，作者认为**可能是** CI-XA 分析中无定形贡献被过度拟合所致 [7]。
- 微晶尺寸由 Scherrer 方程算出；因未扣除仪器展宽，计算值**可能低于**真实值 [8]。
- **以下是我的推断，并非本文内容，也未经本次证据验证**：纤维素 II 的主峰位置与 I 型不同，把基于 Iβ (200) 的指数直接用于 II 型样品，可能得到失真的"表观结晶度"。若你的资料来源确实发生了 I→II 转变，需要核对该来源的晶型判定与结晶度算法是否匹配，而不能沿用本文的数值。

## 更正后的结论

**① 0.919 / 0.925 对应的对象是错的：它们是 CI-XI 与 CI-XA 之间的相关系数，并非氢键含量与 CI-XI 之间的相关系数。**
原文：“the CI-XI and the CI-XA were correlated significantly for both softwood fibers and hardwood fibers, with a correlation coefficient of 0.919 (p < 0.05) for softwood fibers and 0.925 (p < 0.05) for hardwood fibers”[1]。CI-XI 是用 XRD 峰**强度比**得到的结晶指数，CI-XA 是用 XRD 峰**面积比**得到的结晶指数，两者都是结晶度的度量[1][5]。文中把 CI-XI 明显高于 CI-XA 解释为可能由分析 CI-XA 时对非晶部分贡献过拟合所致，这是一种推测（“might be caused”）[1]。

**② 氢键含量与 CI-XI 的真实相关系数是：软木 0.912、阔叶木 0.889（均 p<0.05），针对的是 O(6)H···O(3′) 分子间氢键的相对含量**[2]。需注意原文内部不一致：摘要给出的是软木 **0.888**、阔叶木 0.889[3]。仅凭现有材料无法判断哪个数值正确，引用时应注明正文 0.912 与摘要 0.888 存在矛盾，或回原文核实。

**③ 因此不能用 CI-XI “直接算出”氢键含量。**
- 作者自己的表述只是趋势推测：“there was a significantly positive correlation between the CI-XI and content of O(6)H···O(3)′ H-bonds… Thus, the trend of the content of O(6)H···O(3)′ H-bonds **might be generally speculated** based on CI-XI while refining”[4]，并没有宣称可以定量换算。
- 在所检索到的章节中，未见任何回归方程或换算公式；这是“检索范围内未见”，不能断言全文一定没有，需要回原文全文核实。
- 这些相关性是在 **PFI 打浆处理中**（0、4000、8000、12000、16000 r 共 5 个水平，每个树种 5 个点）内部得到的[5][6]；据表 1、表 2 推断，每树种只有 5 个配对点，样本量很小，r≈0.9 足以说明趋势一致，但不足以支撑外推到其他原料或打浆条件（此为统计判断，不是原文结论）。
- 该“氢键含量”是 FT-IR 羟基谱带（3000–3700 cm⁻¹）去卷积后按峰面积占比得到的**相对含量**[6]，因此不是绝对含量；相关也不等于因果。
- 并且并不是所有氢键都能由 CI-XI 代表：O(2)H···O(6) 与自由 OH(2)/OH(6) 在晶区与非晶区差别较小，与 CI-XI 的相关性“poor”；O(3)H···O(5) 被认为稳定、变化很小，本文未讨论其与 CI-XI 的相关性[2]。作者把 O(6)H···O(3′) 与 CI-XI 趋势相似归因于结晶区该类氢键含量高于非晶区[2]，这属于机理推测（“might be because”）。

**④ 建议表述**：“CI-XI 与 CI-XA 高度相关（软木 0.919、阔叶木 0.925，p<0.05）[1]；CI-XI 与 O(6)H···O(3′) 分子间氢键相对含量显著正相关（正文：软木 0.912、阔叶木 0.889；摘要：0.888/0.889）[2][3]。作者据此仅提出可用 CI-XI 大致推测该氢键含量的变化趋势[4]，并未建立定量换算关系，不宜作为由 CI-XI 计算氢键含量的依据。”

**未解决的信息缺口**：正文与摘要中软木相关系数不一致（0.912 vs 0.888）的原因；以及全文是否给出过回归方程，现有证据不足以判断。

The results showed that the polymorph, H-bonding distance, and H-bonding energy of various H-bonds remained almost unchanged, while the crystalline index, crystallite size, and content of various H-bonds changed with refining. Therein, the content of the inter-molecular O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>) H-bonds was significantly correlated with the crystalline index that was obtained in intensities of the XRD peaks. The Pearson correlation coeficient between them was 0.888 (p < 0.05) for softwood fibers and 0.889 (p < 0.05) for hardwood fibers, respectively. It can be concluded that the variations of accessibility, swelling, and fibrillation were closely related to the supramolecular structure and the intermolecular H-bonds play an important role in the crystal packing of cellulose.

[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction
[原文]
There is still a lack of literature on the efects of PFI refinement on the H-bonding network. Particularly, the relationship between the content of H-bonds and crystallinity is still worthy of further study, which will deepen the understanding of the molecular aggregation and distribution of H-bonds, providing a molecular-scale explanation for the variations in accessibility, swelling, flexibility, and fibrillation of cellulosic fibers during PFI refinement. Therefore, this work explored the efects of PFI refinement on the CI, crystallite size, energy of H-bonds, H-bonding distance, and content of H-bonds for softwood pulp fibers and hardwood pulp fibers. Attempts were made in order to establish the correlations between the CI and content of various H-bonds.

Abstract: Supramolecular structure is the critical factor that afects the properties of cellulosic fibers. This article studied the action of Papirindustriens forskningsinstitut (PFI) refining on the molecular aggregation and hydrogen bonding network, and tried to explore the relationship between the crystal packing and hydrogen-bonding network in cellulosic fibers. The results showed that the polymorph, H-bonding distance, and H-bonding energy of various H-bonds remained almost unchanged, while the crystalline index, crystallite size, and content of various H-bonds changed with refining. Therein, the content of the inter-molecular O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>) H-bonds was significantly correlated with the crystalline index that was obtained in intensities of the XRD peaks. The Pearson correlation coeficient between them was 0.888 (p < 0.05) for softwood fibers and 0.889 (p < 0.05) for hardwood fibers, respectively. It can be concluded that the variations of accessibility, swelling, and fibrillation were closely related to the supramolecular structure and the intermolecular H-bonds play an important role in the crystal packing of cellulose.

## 更正后的结论

**① 0.919 / 0.925 对应的对象是错的：它们是 CI-XI 与 CI-XA 之间的相关系数，并非氢键含量与 CI-XI 之间的相关系数。**
原文：“the CI-XI and the CI-XA were correlated significantly for both softwood fibers and hardwood fibers, with a correlation coefficient of 0.919 (p < 0.05) for softwood fibers and 0.925 (p < 0.05) for hardwood fibers”[1]。CI-XI 是用 XRD 峰**强度比**得到的结晶指数，CI-XA 是用 XRD 峰**面积比**得到的结晶指数，两者都是结晶度的度量[1][5]。文中把 CI-XI 明显高于 CI-XA 解释为可能由分析 CI-XA 时对非晶部分贡献过拟合所致，这是一种推测（“might be caused”）[1]。
**② 氢键含量与 CI-XI 的真实相关系数是：软木 0.912、阔叶木 0.889（均 p<0.05），针对的是 O(6)H···O(3′) 分子间氢键的相对含量**[2]。需注意原文内部不一致：摘要给出的是软木 **0.888**、阔叶木 0.889[3]。仅凭现有材料无法判断哪个数值正确，引用时应注明正文 0.912 与摘要 0.888 存在矛盾，或回原文核实。

**③ 因此不能用 CI-XI “直接算出”氢键含量。**
- 作者自己的表述只是趋势推测：“there was a significantly positive correlation between the CI-XI and content of O(6)H···O(3)′ H-bonds… Thus, the trend of the content of O(6)H···O(3)′ H-bonds **might be generally speculated** based on CI-XI while refining”[4]，并没有宣称可以定量换算。
- 在所检索到的章节中，未见任何回归方程或换算公式；这是“检索范围内未见”，不能断言全文一定没有，需要回原文全文核实。
- 这些相关性是在 **PFI 打浆处理中**（0、4000、8000、12000、16000 r 共 5 个水平，每个树种 5 个点）内部得到的[5][6]；据表 1、表 2 推断，每树种只有 5 个配对点，样本量很小，r≈0.9 足以说明趋势一致，但不足以支撑外推到其他原料或打浆条件（此为统计判断，不是原文结论）。
- 该“氢键含量”是 FT-IR 羟基谱带（3000–3700 cm⁻¹）去卷积后按峰面积占比得到的**相对含量**[6]，因此不是绝对含量；相关也不等于因果。
- 并且并不是所有氢键都能由 CI-XI 代表：O(2)H···O(6) 与自由 OH(2)/OH(6) 在晶区与非晶区差别较小，与 CI-XI 的相关性“poor”；O(3)H···O(5) 被认为稳定、变化很小，本文未讨论其与 CI-XI 的相关性[2]。作者把 O(6)H···O(3′) 与 CI-XI 趋势相似归因于结晶区该类氢键含量高于非晶区[2]，这属于机理推测（“might be because”）。

**④ 建议表述**：“CI-XI 与 CI-XA 高度相关（软木 0.919、阔叶木 0.925，p<0.05）[1]；CI-XI 与 O(6)H···O(3′) 分子间氢键相对含量显著正相关（正文：软木 0.912、阔叶木 0.889；摘要：0.888/0.889）[2][3]。作者据此仅提出可用 CI-XI 大致推测该氢键含量的变化趋势[4]，并未建立定量换算关系，不宜作为由 CI-XI 计算氢键含量的依据。”
**未解决的信息缺口**：正文与摘要中软木相关系数不一致（0.912 vs 0.888）的原因；以及全文是否给出过回归方程，现有证据不足以判断。
